top_findings.claim: The Workspace BDUF's environment vocabulary contradicts the canonical environment sequence used by the other three documents: Workspace section 22.4 defines Local/Preview/Staging/Production while the Baseline (sections 5 and 21), Control Room (section 11), and Mature End State (sections 7 and 16) define Local/Rehearsal/Staging/Production, and PROP-003 rules on Staging without resolving where Preview sits.

top_findings.required_change: Amend Workspace 22.4 to the canonical four-environment sequence and, if per-branch Preview deployments are retained, define Preview explicitly as a disposable Rehearsal-class sub-environment with the same isolation invariants, so no contract or UI ever treats Preview as a fifth authority class.

top_findings.claim: The council disposition vocabulary is inconsistent between the two contracts that govern this very meeting: control-room/contracts/council-review.v1.json allows accept_recommendation | choose_alternative | defer_with_named_external_blocker while the ledger template allows accept | modify | defer_with_named_reopen_trigger | reject; PROP-006 fixes only the deferral value, leaving accept/modify/reject unmapped.
top_findings.required_change: Extend PROP-006's contract change to unify the complete disposition enum (one canonical vocabulary plus an explicit mapping for historical values), applied to control-room/contracts/council-review.v1.json, the Workspace council register, and every council output template in the roadmaps.

rubric_scores.reason: Server-derived immutable identity dimensions (tenant, sponsor, runtime principal, capability, personal-brain scope) are consistent across all four documents and both contract suites, with live spoof-refusal evidence (partner=dell refused, loop 319 closed) and deny-before-disclosure fixtures for tenant, workspace, and cross-brain paths.

One canonical record layer with projections everywhere (Salesforce as provenance, maps/renders/exports as projections), Unknown-never-Healthy semantics enforced in contracts, fixtures, prototype code (Mixed/Partial counts, unlocated queues), and the surface-registry/cutover discipline resists shadow systems structurally.

The adoption architecture (AI-session displacement test, five baselines with bound actions, uncoached-journey gates, canonical item grammar) is the strongest I have reviewed at this scale, but zero human evidence exists: all twelve uncoached journeys are unperformed and all five baselines are unmeasured, so adoption remains a thesis, not a result. Bounded follow-up: perform them before Phase 0 exit as already required.

Sequencing (council -> release truth -> environments -> CI -> reads -> workflows -> read-first Control Room -> gated mutation) is coherent and evidence-gated, and PROP-002/003 repair the real Phase 0/Phase 1 seam; held at 3 for the stale calendar anchors in Mature s30, the Preview/Rehearsal vocabulary conflict, and the amendment-application risk of landing nine ordered amendment groups as one consistent revision.

Claim labels are used honestly (known_open_evidence lists the unfixed ordinal-2 defect rather than hiding it), machine evidence reproduces (35/35, 94/94, validator green re-run at the frozen commit), fact corrections FACT-001..007 separate dated observations from contract constants, and the ROI hypothesis even documents that its own bottom-up numbers fail the top-down arithmetic check.

Vendor pricing is dated, sourced, and gated by purchase triggers, and the Hermes credit mechanics correction is exactly right; held at 3 because every band remains unmeasured hypothesis, the five operating baselines that anchor ROI are null, and dated Claude/ChatGPT seat comparisons will drift fastest of all the evidence in the set.

Tenant-readiness and the 150-plus human seat architecture are pre-engineered exactly where retrofit would be expensive (identity, isolation, audit, search, offline) while every commercialization surface (signup, billing, portal, marketplace, generic workflow engine) stays excluded with an explicit three-approved-workflows extraction bar.

strongest_remaining_objections: Zero human acceptance evidence exists anywhere in the program: all twelve uncoached journeys are unperformed and all five displacement baselines are unmeasured, so every adoption claim in all four documents is currently a well-structured hypothesis; the council must not let architectural quality read as validated adoption.

The approval will trigger nine ordered amendment groups across four doctrine documents plus two contract suites; if these land piecemeal or out of order, the cross-document consistency this council just verified degrades immediately — the amendment pass itself needs the same one-controlled-revision discipline and re-verification the packet demanded of the sources.

The Hermes evaluation introduces the system's first standing third-party runtime holding CARR-scoped credentials on preview-grade hosting, where the vendor's isolation claim is explicitly unverified and the negative-verification burden falls on a two-person firm; the R0 gates are right, but slippage from 'evaluation' to 'quiet dependency' is the likeliest failure path and deserves a named tripwire (any Hermes-mediated routine that Joe starts relying on before the graduation gates is a stop condition, not a success signal).
evidence_that_would_change_view: Joe's twelve uncoached journey results (pass or fail) — failures would convert RUB-ADOPT findings into required product changes before Phase 1 feature work.
Portal Cloud negative isolation tests failing — would flip PROP-007 from Portal-hosted to self-hosted-or-defer.
Measured OAuth/KV write instrumentation showing paid-tier headroom insufficient — would reopen the auth state-store design before Phase 1.
The 48-hour disconnected-Drive test surfacing an uninventoried consumer — would extend PROP-010's transition inventory and delay any Drive-free claim.
A trademark/domain screen eliminating all viable independent names quickly — would not reverse PROP-008's architecture but would extend the interim alias period.
